note: Names, descriptions and grades are as PlayStation publishes them (Exophase and PSNProfiles agree). Every guide below is our own advice from the official description; exact places are not yet checked in the game where the guide says so.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are yours — there is nothing extra to do for it. Work the roadmap in order (story, strands, activities, collectibles) and use this tracker to see what is left; the last trophy you earn hands you this one with it. If you are one trophy short, filter the checklist to Unearned and the missing one is your whole job list.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing the opening mission, Gone Fishing. Start a new game and play the prologue through to its end; the trophy pops as the mission completes. It cannot be missed — every save passes through this mission — and it is the natural first tick on the checklist.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded when Chapter 1 of the story is finished. Keep following the main mission markers until the chapter closes; there is no side condition. Not missable. While you are in Chapter 1, start noting collectible spots and activity icons on the map — the roadmap's later stages lean on them, and you will thank yourself for the early pins.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Awarded when Chapter 2 of the story is finished, name exactly as PlayStation publishes it (asterisks included). Play the main missions to the chapter's end; no extra requirement. Not missable. Chapter 2 is a good point to begin the stranger strands and the named-character chains (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) so they are not all waiting at the end.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Awarded when Chapter 3 of the story is finished. Follow the main missions to the chapter's end. Not missable. By now most of Leonida should be open to you, so this is the point where the roadmap shifts weight: finish the story, but start clearing activities and collectibles between missions instead of saving everything for cleanup.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Awarded when Chapter 4 of the story is finished. Play the main missions through to the chapter's close. Not missable. After Chapter 4 only the final mission stands between you and the end of the story — before you run it, check the Missables view: finish the character strands first, in case the finale locks any of them (that lock is not yet checked in the game, so the safe order costs nothing).

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Gold trophy for completing the story's final mission. It ends Stage 1 of the roadmap. Before starting it, clear the flagged missables — the five named-character finales and the stranger strands — because a finale can lock side content in this series and whether it does here is not yet checked in the game. Keep a separate save before the final mission either way; it is the cheapest insurance on the whole list.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Story trophy tied to one named mission: Breakfast Run. When the mission appears in your story progress, play it to completion and the trophy pops. Not missable on the description's wording — it is a completion award, not a performance award — but if the mission offers a choice, note what you picked; Actions Speak Louder tracks choices separately.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

Heists in this series usually feed money trophies, so after it lands, check your totals toward Dime on the Dollar ($250,000 laundered) and Treat Yo Self ($100,000 spent) — both are cheaper to finish while story money is flowing.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

If a choice appears inside it, write the pick in this trophy's note field — the choice-count trophy (Actions Speak Louder) makes a running log useful.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the named mission Headliners. Play it to the end; nothing in the description asks for a particular approach. Not missable. Keep an eye out during story missions for one-off moments the vague trophies point at (Personal Best, The Truth Is Out There) — if something odd happens on screen, check the checklist before moving on.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

VCIA also appears in Catch Me If You Can (an unscheduled departure at VCIA) — while this mission puts you at VCIA, look around for what an unscheduled departure could mean, and note it; the exact trigger is not yet checked in the game.

Late-story missions are the natural home of the combat trophy Gunslinger (5 takedowns in one Combat Focus) — if a big firefight offers a crowd, that is your moment to try it.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Gold trophy for reaching 100% game completion — the in-game completion percentage, not just the trophy list. That means the story, the strands, the activities and the collectibles the game counts toward 100%, which overlaps heavily with this roadmap but may not match it exactly; the game's own completion checklist (wherever it shows it) is the authority, and its exact contents are not yet checked in the game. Use the counter here to mirror the percentage the game reports, and treat this as the last big target before the platinum.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 250 stunts in total. Stunts are the game's stunt jumps and stunt moments; the description counts completions, so find a reliable jump you can repeat and farm it, or collect them naturally while driving between objectives — 250 is a grind either way, so start early and let travel do the work. Track your count in the counter here against the total the game reports. Not missable: stunts stay available in free roam.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity at least once — PSN tracks 9 activity types for this one. You do not need to win or finish them, just start each type once: races, drone races, fishing, bowling, the arcade, the shooting range and the rest as the map reveals them. The full list of the 9 types is not yet checked in the game, so tick them off in the note field as you try each new icon; when the counter reaches 9 the trophy should pop. Not missable.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — PSN counts 42 of them. Work through the range's challenge list weapon by weapon; gold usually means beating a score or time bar, so replay a challenge until the medal upgrades, then move on. Keep the counter here in step with your gold count (42 golds = done). The range's location and each challenge's gold bar are not yet checked in the game. Not missable: the range stays open for retries.

Visit each drone-race start point on the map and win once at each; a win at the same location twice does not advance the count. Note each location in the note field as you clear it so the last few are easy to find. The 14 locations are not yet checked in the game. Not missable.

Not missable.

The 18 locations are not yet checked in the game; pair the sweep with The Goodtime State (explore all 52 areas) so one tour of the map clears both. Not missable.

trophies.guide: Hunt one specific, unique animal for the character Bret. trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are gathered in the world (and possibly bought or won — the method is not yet checked in the game); a set counts only when every card in it is collected, so track set by set in the note field rather than by raw card count. Three complete sets earn the trophy; partial sets earn nothing. Not missable on the description's wording, but start collecting early — sets are slow.

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for using the WAiNK It action at 100 different locations. Treat it as a collectible sweep: whenever you reach a new named place, WAiNK It there once and bump the counter. Repeat visits to the same location should not count, so log places in the note field as you go. What WAiNK It does in-world and which spots qualify are not yet checked in the game. Not missable; pair it with the exploration sweep.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges in total. Challenges are the game's tracked mini-objectives (the list lives in the game's menus — its exact contents are not yet checked in the game). Pick the quick ones first, keep the counter here in step with the game's own total, and let story play knock out the incidental ones. Not missable.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner with you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape clean. Both halves matter: the partner must be present, and you must actually shake the heat rather than die or get busted. Flagged missable as a precaution: partner availability can depend on story progress, and when your partner is free to roam with you is not yet checked in the game. Plan it for a free-roam stretch, save first, and use a hideout or vehicle swap to break line of sight.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level alive the whole time — if the heat drops between shops, the chain breaks. Pick three shops close together, rob one to raise the wanted level, then move straight to the next without hiding long enough to lose it. Flagged missable as a precaution for the same partner-availability reason as Hot Together, which is not yet checked in the game. Do both partner trophies in the same free-roam session and save beforehand.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovery usually means encountering, entering or registering a vehicle type for the first time; the exact trigger is not yet checked in the game, so drive everything you see — steal, borrow and buy widely instead of sticking to one car. Keep the counter in step with the game's vehicle log. Pairs naturally with On the Spot (register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app). Not missable.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of the Combat Focus ability. Save the ability for a crowded firefight — a story shootout or a gang operation with plenty of targets in view — activate Combat Focus once, and drop five before it ends. If you only get three or four, the attempt fails; reload or wait for the next crowd. How Combat Focus is unlocked and how long it lasts are not yet checked in the game. Not missable: crowds keep coming.

trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — leave the VCIA site by a route or method that is not the normal exit. The description is deliberately vague and the exact trigger is not yet checked in the game: when story business takes you to VCIA (see Hi-Jacked), explore for an unofficial way out — a vehicle, a restricted door, a fence line — and try leaving that way. trophies.guide: The description only jokes about Rhinos (the series' tank), so the real trigger is not pinned down by the official text — most likely it involves a Rhino encounter: getting into one, stealing one, or surviving one. It is not yet checked in the game. Practical approach: when a Rhino appears (a high wanted level or a military-flavoured mission are the usual sources), interact with it rather than fleeing — enter it if you can — and check whether the trophy pops. Flagged missable as a precaution in case the Rhino moment is a one-off story beat; keep a save before military missions.

trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery: get in, take the goods, and get out without raising an alarm or a wanted level. Scout the store first for cameras, guards and a quiet entry; if you are spotted, leave and retry rather than fighting, since detection is what fails it. Which stores qualify and how detection is judged are not yet checked in the game. Not missable: stores stay open for another attempt.

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for robbing 5 bank vaults and escaping each time. The escape is part of the requirement: a vault robbery that ends in death or arrest should not count, so plan the getaway before you start — a fast vehicle nearby and a route that breaks line of sight. Five separate vaults; repeat-robbing the same bank may or may not count, so log each bank in the note field. Vault locations and cooldowns are not yet checked in the game. Not missable.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Watch for armored trucks on the road, stop or disable one, take the money, and lose any wanted level that follows — the escape is required, not optional. A fast getaway vehicle and a quiet place to ditch the heat make it routine. Truck routes and spawn habits are not yet checked in the game. Not missable: trucks keep driving.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — PSN counts 52 areas. Drive, fly or boat into every named area at least once until the map's area list is complete; the fog-of-war style map usually reveals an area when you enter it. Do this as one grand tour in Stage 4 and combine it with the meditation spots (18), the WAiNK locations (100) and vehicle discovery (100) so a single sweep feeds four trophies. The 52 area names are not yet checked in the game; log them in the note field as you enter each one. Not missable.

sources.label: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

Log the gang names in the note field as you clear them; the nine gangs and their operation locations are not yet checked in the game. These robberies also build wanted levels, so they pair with the escape trophies. Not missable.

One of the 9 activity types for Master of None may be social drinking — this could cover it. Not missable.

trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks this one to a count of 500.
